title: Spectral product noise operator
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the $\pi$-weighted inner product, indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. Suppose one basis vector, indexed by $a_0$, is the constant-one function. For $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$, its spectral product noise transform at $x\in\Omega^n$ is the sum over product-basis indices $a\in\iota^n$ of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ times the product-basis function at $x$, weighted by $\rho^{|a|}$, where $|a|$ counts the coordinates of $a$ that differ from $a_0$.
